Card.Name: NTFS Last Access Time Updates
Card.Description: Windows can update a file or directory's last-access timestamp when it is accessed. Disabling these updates can reduce some disk overhead, but software that depends on last-access data can lose that signal.
Card.FriendlyDescription: Windows can update a file or directory's last-access timestamp when it is accessed. Disabling these updates can reduce some disk overhead, but software that depends on last-access data can lose that signal.
Card.WhatWeKnowSummary: Claim: Windows can update a file or directory's last-access timestamp when it is accessed. Disabling these updates can reduce some disk overhead, but software that depends on last-access data can lose that signal. Evidence: Microsoft's web-server performance guidance provides the exact registry path and modern default of 1. The matching fsutil behavior documentation states that disablelastaccess {1|0} disables (1) or enables (0) updates to the Last Access Time stamp. Rollback: Rollback: Verified via record-restore-story.
